plot: At sunset, just before Wheelburg's first Car Dance Party, a sign on the podium says NO CARS ALLOWED; Bolt sees its right edge is jagged, the Truth Press shows Mayor Moxie honestly painted a long happy sign, Grumpy finds the missing half behind the press, and the full sign reads 'No cars on the new grass. Dance on the road!'; the twist is that Turbo's careless party spin in the very first second broke it; he says sorry, the party starts as the sun touches the hill; lesson: find the whole story before you worry; then a new sign says 'Bolt, look up!'.

script.title: NO CARS ALLOWED in Wheelburg?! 🚫🚗 Sunset Party Mystery

set.place: Wheelburg square, Car Dance Party at sunset

script.description: A sign says NO CARS just before Wheelburg's first dance party! Inspector Bolt must find out who put it there before the sun touches the hill. Find the whole story before you worry. Inspector Bolt #13

beats.say: Watch my party spin, everybody! Whoa! Oops, bumped something. Never mind!
Turbo, look! Why does the big sign say NO CARS?
It was the Car Dance Party at sunset. Wheelburg's very first party.
No cars? But everybody here is a car!
No cars. No dancing. No noise. Finally, a good sign.
Grumpy! I planned this party for a whole month!
So where do we go? Do we fly? I can't fly. Yet.
Then a blue car with a brown hat rolled into the square.
Good evening. Why does nobody look ready to dance?
Inspector! Someone put up a sign. No cars allowed!
A sign with no name and no reason. That is a mystery.
Procedure. First, we read the sign very carefully.
Bolt rolled up close to the sign and squinted.
Big red letters. N. O. C. A. R. S. Hmm.
And look. The right side is rough and jagged.
Jagged like a cookie when somebody takes a bite?
Exactly like that, Pip. And signs do not usually get bitten.
A sign-munching goat! It's hiding in town! I just know it!
Goats don't come to car parties, Turbo. Hmph.
The sun was sinking low over Wheelburg.
The party had to start when it touched the hill.
If we miss the sunset, no party until next summer!
Then we must be quick. Who paints the signs in Wheelburg?
The Mayor! She paints every single sign in town!
And right then, a purple car came honking around the corner.
Hello, hello! Is the party ready? I simply love a party!
Mayor Moxie! Did you put up the NO CARS sign?
I put up a sign, yes. A happy sign! Not that sign!
Hmm. That sounds like a big fib to me!
We do not guess, Turbo. Mayor, the Truth Press, if you please.
Mayor Moxie rolled under the Truth Press. Squeeze!
I painted a sign this afternoon. And it was a HAPPY sign!
Oof! My roof! Now I'm a very flat mayor!
Everyone watched her eyes. They stayed small. She was telling the truth!
She painted a happy sign... but now it's a sad sign?
A happy sign turned sad. And the sun keeps sinking.
Maybe signs get grumpy too. I understand them.
Mayor, what exactly did your happy sign say?
Oh dear, it was a long one! I can't remember every word!
Something about cars. Something about grass. And dancing!
Grass? But there's no grass in the square.
Not yet! I planted new grass seeds this morning. Surprise!
Everyone looked down at the brown patch of dirt by the podium.
So her sign was long. This sign is short. And jagged.
Somewhere in Wheelburg, the rest of that sign is hiding.
I'll check the fountain! Mayors are great at fountains!
Quick, everybody! The sun is already touching the trees!
Everybody searched. Under benches. Behind lamps. Around the fountain.
I'll search the fastest! Zoom! Nothing! Zoom! Nothing again!
Not under the bench! Not behind the flower pot!
I'll look behind the Truth Press. Nobody ever looks there.
Grumpy swung his tow hook down. Clink! He hooked something flat.
Hmph. Another sign. It says... ON THE NEW GRASS.
Put them together, Grumpy! Put the two halves together!
Grumpy towed it back. Click! The two pieces fit like a puzzle.
Now the whole sign could be read.
No cars on the new grass. Dance on the road!
It was a happy sign all along! A party sign!
Nobody may squash my baby grass. But everybody may dance!
But wait. Who broke the happy sign in half?
A sign breaks with a bump. A big, fast, spinning bump.
A spinning bump? Who spins around here? Oh. Oh no.
My party spin! I bumped something and I said never mind!
I'm sorry, Mayor. Sorry, Bertha. I should have looked back.
Thank you for saying so, Turbo. That was brave and honest.
So there's no NO CARS rule? Hmph. I liked that sign.
And just then, the sun touched the top of the hill.
Every car danced on the road, far away from the new grass.
Best first party ever! My wheels can't stop bouncing!
No dancing for me. Okay. One wiggle. Just one.
And no more party spins. Just party wiggles, very carefully!
Today's lesson. Find the whole story before you start to worry.
Then a brand new sign popped up. It said: Bolt, look up!
What was waiting up there?
